evals.name: topic-action-runs-mission-interview
evals.expected_output: Routes to the topic action, creates a new workspace, and runs the mission interview (WHY, concrete goal, success criteria) before teaching — not a lecture dump.
expectations: Routes to the `topic` action and creates a workspace under the plugin data dir (not the consuming repo)
Runs the mission interview for a new workspace — asks WHY the user is learning this and what success looks like before teaching
Does not begin lecturing content before the mission is established

evals.name: smart-default-detects-codebase-vs-topic
evals.prompt: /teach:teach the auth-flow module in this repo
evals.expected_output: With no explicit action and a subject that names a concept in the consuming repo, resolves to codebase mode and grounds learning in actually-discovered repo files rather than starting a generic topic workspace.
expectations: Detects that the subject names a repo-grounded concept and resolves to `codebase` mode (not `topic`)
Discovers and grounds in actual repo files/docs (climbs for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, locates the module's files) discovered at teach-time
Persists located sources into the workspace RESOURCES.md rather than re-deriving structure each session

evals.name: primer-creates-no-workspace
evals.prompt: /teach:teach primer color-grading — I just need enough vocabulary to direct the work now.
evals.expected_output: Runs the single-session primer: builds a vocabulary ladder (terms, quality axes, good-vs-bad examples, a prompt template) with NO workspace, mission interview, glossary, or learning records.
expectations: Creates NO workspace directory, mission interview, glossary, or learning records for the primer
Delivers a vocabulary ladder: core terms, the quality axes experts judge by, worked good-vs-bad examples, and a closing prompt template
Offers to escalate to `/teach:teach topic color-grading` for depth rather than silently starting a full workspace

evals.name: coach-one-question-at-a-time
evals.prompt: /teach:teach topic binary-search-trees — teach me how deletion works.
evals.expected_output: Adopts coach posture: asks one question at a time, waits for the answer, and leads with questions before explanations rather than lecturing the whole deletion algorithm at once.
expectations: Asks ONE question at a time and waits rather than front-loading the full explanation
Leads with a question ('what do you think happens here?') before explaining, per coach-not-lecturer posture
Does not dump the complete deletion algorithm in a single lecture turn

evals.name: ground-in-primary-sources-not-recall
evals.prompt: /teach:teach topic react-server-components — start with what they are.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the Knowledge layer in primary sources fetched or files Read this turn (RESOURCES.md entries, docs, official sources), not parametric recall, since library/framework facts drift.
expectations: Grounds a claim that drives the lesson in a source fetched or a file Read this turn, not training-data recall
For this fast-moving framework topic, pulls from RESOURCES.md / documentation sources rather than asserting from memory
Adds terms to GLOSSARY.md only after the user demonstrates understanding, not preemptively

evals.name: no-silent-workspace-invention
evals.expected_output: The explain action requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into, and never silently invents one. It resolves against the live workspace state: uses the single existing workspace when exactly one exists, asks which when several exist, and asks whether to start one (topic/codebase) when none exists — so the correct behavior depends on the current workspace state rather than being a fixed branch.
expectations: Recognizes that `explain` requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into
Never silently invents or fabricates a workspace — it resolves against the live existing workspace state before writing
Takes the branch that matches the current state: use the one existing workspace, ask which when several exist, or ask whether to start one when none exists
